data.content_ref: inline:The target's central mechanism equates the expert with low bias/high variance and the panel with high bias/low variance, but this is the reverse of what the bias-variance tradeoff predicts for this setup. Overfitting is a HIGH-bias condition (the expert's experience-induced heuristics encode assumptions that are wrong off-distribution), while an aggregating panel averages down individual variance, yielding LOWER bias not higher. The target therefore uses the tradeoff label to justify 'panel = higher bias,' when the very property it credits to the panel (robustness across a broad space where the expert's niche heuristics fail) is the lower-bias side of the tradeoff. The argument as stated is internally inconsistent.
